acceptance.criterion: Synthetic secret absent from JSON, text resource and error; JSON preserves safe fields and numeric schema. Unsafe secret-bearing numeric representation gives format-unsafe.
acceptance.evidence: Three MCP runtime tests cover parseable operation JSON with sibling redaction metadata, a required numeric secret producing a leak-safe format-unsafe error, and tool-error/resource redaction. Tests currently fail on invalid JSON, missing state, incorrect success, and raw resource content.

acceptance.criterion: Safe IDs/metrics remain, true secrets cannot bypass through field name. Sensitive URL query/path redacted; plain public Markdown link alone not exfiltration.
acceptance.evidence: Two security-service/detector tests preserve safe IDs, counts and decimal metrics while requiring secrets under id/metric keys to be masked. URL path/query masking is a passing positive control; the same scenario remains RED because a plain public documentation link is incorrectly classified as egress.

acceptance.criterion: Recursive nested scan works, symlink cycles terminate, required inaccessible/limit cases are incomplete while findings retained.
acceptance.evidence: Three CLI runtime tests cover default recursive traversal, canonical internal links and cycles, external/unreadable entries, leak-safe per-file results, max-files/max-bytes bounds, and FAIL with independently incomplete coverage. All currently reproduce EISDIR.
